head: b3edfa2e5522bee094eca6e694ce867ffd23d987
summary:
Attempt 2 (b3edfa2) changed only `.taad/fitness.yaml`: the header, plus `﻿?` after `^` in the two screen-rule patterns. The file is blob 179373b, 7704 bytes, all ASCII, tracked and not gitignored.

**Fitness MCP tool in this worktree:** op=check reports "8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds." It gave the same text before and after a full-suite build (86/86 pass). op=rules lists all 8 rooted entries.

**Engine module on scratch copies.** I ran the engine's fitness module in-process (taad_v3 f53813a; fitness.py and design.py are unchanged since 0260e7e) against copies of `git ls-files` under %TEMP%\sl022-val2.
- **Planted copy:** 16 violations. Fitness and xUnit report the identical (Fact, file, line) set, with nothing missing and nothing extra. The set includes a using directive at Scanner.cs:7, comment-only DllImport and LibraryImport, csproj and xaml hits, the widened reparse rule in App and LongPath.cs, Skip, Explicit and SkipException, and three line-1 plants:
  - a BOM plus `using System.Windows;`
  - a BOM plus an indented `using static FsAnalyser.App.X;`
  - a no-BOM `using PresentationFramework;`
- **O-007:** its behaviour is fixed. A BOM file with `using System.IO;` fires in neither engine.
- **Exempt files:** tokens planted in Kernel32.cs, EntryClassifier.cs and TestNative.cs fire in neither engine.
- **Built copy:** it has bin/obj, WPF MainWindow.g.cs, LibraryImports.g.cs, and junk planted in .dotnet/, artifacts/, TestResults/, bin/ and obj/. With the new yaml it still passes: 8 rules, 33 files, 0 unmatched.
- **Controls:** a typo'd glob is listed as unmatched, a tree with no yaml reads NONE, and a `$` probe fires on a CRLF file.
- **Engine append:** the committed `_append_rules` keeps the 7704 bytes as an exact prefix and gives 9 rules, and the check still passes.

**Two things keep this from a pass:**
1. **O-008 is still open and I measured it true.** It is owed to build-slice. Header lines 15-16 still promise that every violation xUnit reports in a UTF-8 file under 2 MB is also reported by Fitness. Line 38 still says Fitness prunes only bin/ and obj/. In a divergence copy, xUnit failed on three plants that Fitness passed with 33 files read:
   - `// DllImport` in src/FsAnalyser.Core/packages/Planted.cs
   - `// 0x400` in src/FsAnalyser.Core/dist/Planted.cs
   - Kernel32.cs renamed to KERNEL32.cs (xUnit's `.Except` is case-sensitive; Fitness's except_files glob is not)

   The two divergences the header does disclose behave as it says: a multi-line `[Fact(...,\n Skip = ...)]` fails Fitness and passes xUnit, and a UTF-16 file fails xUnit and passes Fitness.
2. **Criterion 13 is not met.** A tree without the file reads NONE. The design predicted this and marked it non-material. No other slice is in flight: `git worktree list` shows only uat and SL-022.

**A pattern across attempts.** This is the second time build-slice has been sent back for a sentence in the yaml header that claims universal parity with xUnit: O-007 in attempt 1, O-008 now. Each review finds a new counterexample. No rule has misbehaved in attempt 2. Fixing O-008 by adding one more item to the list leaves the same claim open to the next counterexample. Saying xUnit is the authority, and listing the divergences as examples rather than as a complete set, would end the pattern.

criteria.criterion: 1. Fitness loads the rule file at validate (committed on the slice branch, \b and \s patterns single-quoted)
criteria.how: The Fitness MCP tool in this worktree: op=rules lists 8 entries with \b, \s and ﻿ intact, and op=check reports 8 rules on 33 files. The file is committed at b3edfa2 (blob 179373b), with 0 double-quoted scalars.

criteria.criterion: 2. The file reaches trunk (not matched by .gitignore)
criteria.how: git check-ignore exits 1 for .taad/fitness.yaml and .taad/, and the file is tracked on the branch. The actual arrival on uat happens at merge, after validate, and was not observed.

criteria.criterion: 3. The screen-free rule fires on a using directive after line 1 (Scanner.cs:7)
criteria.how: Planted copy: Fitness reported 'TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen (*.cs)' at Scanner.cs:7, and xUnit reported the same file:line. The three line-1 shapes (BOM, BOM plus indented using static, no BOM) also fired in both engines.

criteria.criterion: 4. The interop rule fires on a banned token inside a // comment
criteria.how: '// planted: DllImport belongs in Native' fired the (src) entry at Scanner.cs:9. '// planted: LibraryImport' fired the (tests) entry at CancellationTests.cs:14. Both matched xUnit, and in_comments was empty.

criteria.criterion: 5. A rule whose xUnit scope spans two file types fires in each (.csproj, .xaml)
criteria.how: UseWPF and a ProjectReference to App fired the (*.csproj) entry at FsAnalyser.Core.csproj:8 and :9. IsReparsePoint fired the (*.xaml) entry at MainWindow.xaml:8. Both matched xUnit.

criteria.criterion: 6. The widened reparse rule fires outside the classifier (App project)
criteria.how: FileAttributes.ReparsePoint and 0x00000400 in MainWindow.xaml.cs fired at :12 and :13 in both engines. 0x400 in Native/LongPath.cs fired at :85, so the reparse exemption is exact to Kernel32.cs.

criteria.criterion: 7. Exempted files legitimately hold the token (Kernel32.cs, EntryClassifier.cs, TestNative.cs)
criteria.how: The clean tree passes. Tokens appended to all three files fired in neither Fitness nor xUnit.

criteria.criterion: 8. A tests/**/*.cs entry runs over ArchitectureRulesTests.cs (with its pattern literals) with comments included
criteria.how: The clean worktree (MCP) and the clean copy pass with including_comments true on every entry. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**/*.cs and tests/**/*.cs cover that file. The globs are unchanged since attempt 1, where per-Fact coverage equalled xUnit's Files() sets.

criteria.criterion: 9. The rooted globs cover their target files (no glob matches nothing)
criteria.how: MCP op=check has no MATCHED NO FILES section, and Report.unmatched is [] on the clean and built copies. The typo control is listed as unmatched.

criteria.criterion: 10. op=check on a built worktree (bin/obj, *.g.cs, .dotnet/, artifacts/, TestResults/)
criteria.how: The built scratch copy, with the new yaml, MainWindow.g.cs, LibraryImports.g.cs and junk violations in all five directories, passes: 8 rules, 33 files. MCP op=check on the real worktree after the full-suite build also passes.

criteria.criterion: 11. A $-anchored pattern matches a CRLF source file
criteria.how: The shipped yaml has no $ pattern, so this is vacuous for the deliverable. A probe rule ending in $ fired at Scanner.cs:7 on a CRLF file.

criteria.criterion: 12. The never-skipped rule fires on a skipped counting test
criteria.how: [Fact(Skip = ...)], [Fact(Explicit = true)] and SkipException in CancellationTests.cs fired at :8, :10 and :13 in both engines.

criteria.criterion: 13. A slice cut before this merges reads the rules
criteria.how: A tree without .taad/fitness.yaml reads NONE (ctl-noyaml). The design marked this material: false as a known limit. Q-010's rule (cut after the merge, or rebase) is the mitigation. No such slice exists now: only the uat and SL-022 worktrees.

criteria.criterion: 14. A later design appends its declared rules onto the hand-written file
criteria.how: The committed taad3.design._append_rules (design.py is unchanged since 0260e7e, HEAD f53813a) kept the 7704-byte file as an exact prefix. It added a 9th rule and check still passes. This was a direct call, not a real design stage.

obligations.evidence: Still open (owed to build-slice) and measured true. Header lines 15-16 still say every violation xUnit reports in a UTF-8 file under 2 MB is also reported by Fitness. Line 38 still says Fitness prunes bin/ and obj/ by name. In %TEMP%\sl022-val2\div, xUnit failed three plants that Fitness passed with 33 files read: InteropLivesOnlyInNative at src/FsAnalyser.Core/packages/Planted.cs:1, and OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute at src/FsAnalyser.Core/dist/Planted.cs:1 and at the case-renamed Native/KERNEL32.cs:23. That KERNEL32 case had previously only been read from the code. It is minor: nothing in the current tree triggers it, and xUnit remains the backstop.

Lines 47 and 57 read '(?m)^﻿?\s*using...'. In the planted copy, a BOM plus line-1 'using System.Windows;' and a BOM plus an indented 'using static FsAnalyser.App.X;' both fired at :1 in Fitness and in xUnit. A BOM plus 'using System.IO;' fired in neither.

6/8 entries equal the xUnit literal plus (?m). The two screen entries equal it with ^ changed to ^﻿?, the transform the m1 decision authorised. The planted run shows identical hit sets in both engines.
Report.unmatched is [] on the clean and built copies. The MCP check has no MATCHED NO FILES section.
git check-ignore -v .taad/fitness.yaml .taad/ exits 1. The file is tracked as blob 179373b.

not_reached: The merge to uat, and a slice cut after it reading 8 rules at its own validate, were not observed. uat does not have the file yet.
A real later design stage with non-empty architecture_rules writing into this file. Only _append_rules was called directly, on a scratch copy.

The planted shapes ran through the engine's fitness module in-process on %TEMP% copies, not through the Fitness MCP path, which reads only this worktree. It is the same module, and the clean-tree text is identical to the MCP output.
How the engine's own gates treat a report whose verdict is 'pass' but whose unmatched list is non-empty (the typo control).
Whether commit-slice, merge and reflect leave the file intact on this real repo. That was measured only in spike 3's scripted-model run.
A covered file over 2 MB was not planted by this validation. It rests on the builder's attempt-2 measurement.
